data.body: Follow-up to B-fix-asagent-claim (89fa18e), which made only ddflow_claim ignore the connection's called_from for a per-call as_agent naming someone else. (1) Every other MCP tool that reads called_from (gate_run, gate_record, review, merge, tests, precommit, heartbeat) still resolved a subagent's call against the PARENT's harness tree: for an item claimed --no-worktree, gate_run ran the parent's tree as the subagent's pass, review diffed the parent's branch, merge landed the parent's branch. Fix: in the dispatcher, a foreign as_agent is asked from the primary for every wants_called_from tool -- the item's bound tree/branch decides; with none, the existing 'name --branch' / unavailable answers apply, as from the CLI in the primary. (2) CLI: 'ddflow --agent X claim' from inside a linked worktree adopted it whatever X was. Rule: adopt only when no --agent was given or --agent equals the identity this invocation would have without it (env, config or tree-derived) -- the same rule MCP applies; otherwise claim as from the primary (a tree of its own). B5c32cbb5c1 (home-simulator) is the same defect as B7c7a0d9222 plus its merge/review consequence, closed here.
data.title: A subagent's identity resolves the item's tree on every surface: MCP gate_run/gate_record/review/merge/tests/precommit/heartbeat under a foreign as_agent ask from the primary, and 'ddflow --agent X claim' adopts the tree it stands in only when X is that tree's own identity (fixes bugs B11e4c5a185, B5c32cbb5c1)

Edge cases checked against 61eb669: an item with its own recorded tree still rebinds to it whoever claims (claim's recorded-tree branch runs before adoption; 'not adopted' line suppressed when rebound); --no-worktree claims are unaffected (no tree, no message); a subagent's MCP heartbeat renews its own lease directly (only the stand-in-the-tree proxy renewal is lost, which was the parent's tree); a named agent alone in a fresh harness tree still adopts (test_a_named_agent_alone_in_a_harness_tree_still_adopts_it, and the existing test_cleanup_respects_leases/test_lease_tree_identity '--agent worker/lead' adoption tests pass). Known limit: an agent that first worked in its tree under the derived id and later passes --agent gets a fresh tree, with a message saying why and how to adopt.

No parallel identity derivation: infra.log.bare_agent_id and the new tree_agent_ids share _host(); the clone suffix is read from the same CLONE_ID_FILE (without creating it). The MCP fix reuses Server._someone_else and removes the claim-only adopts_callers_tree flag rather than adding per-tool flags. services.identity (pre-B190 rehome) is a different concern.

data.body: Follow-up to B-fix-asagent-claim (89fa18e), which made only ddflow_claim ignore the connection's called_from for a per-call as_agent naming someone else. (1) MCP: every other tool that reads called_from (gate_run, gate_record, review, merge, tests, precommit, heartbeat) still resolved a subagent's call against the PARENT's harness tree: for an item claimed --no-worktree, gate_run ran the parent's tree as the subagent's pass and merge landed the parent's branch. Fix: the dispatcher asks every wants_called_from tool from the primary for a foreign as_agent -- the item's own tree/branch decides; with none, the existing 'name --branch' / unavailable answers apply, as from the CLI in the primary. MCP knows the connection's identity, so this is unconditional. (2) CLI: 'ddflow --agent X claim' from a linked worktree adopted it whatever X was. The CLI has no connection identity, and a named agent adopting its OWN harness-isolated tree is established, tested behaviour (test_cleanup_respects_leases, test_lease_tree_identity claim with --agent worker/lead from a harness tree and expect adoption) -- so 'never adopt under a foreign --agent' is not an option. Rule: the tree is someone else's when the identity derived from it is not the caller AND that identity has written to the log (somebody works there under it -- the parent session's case); then the claim is answered as from the primary (a tree of its own) and says 'not adopted: ...'. No --agent, --agent naming the tree's identity, or a named agent in a tree whose derived identity never wrote, still adopt. Known limit: a tree whose occupant has never written under its derived identity is indistinguishable from a harness-isolated agent's fresh tree. B5c32cbb5c1 (home-simulator) is the same defect as B7c7a0d9222 plus its merge/review consequence.
data.title: A subagent's identity resolves the item's tree on every surface: MCP tools under a foreign as_agent ask from the primary, and 'ddflow --agent X claim' does not adopt a tree another identity is working in (fixes bugs B11e4c5a185, B5c32cbb5c1)

data.summary: CLI cannot tell a parent's harness tree from a subagent's own when the parent uses a DECLARED identity. B-fix-asagent-tree (services/tree_owner.py) treats a linked tree as another identity's only when the identity DERIVED from it has written to the log. A parent session that always passes --agent/DDFLOW_AGENT never writes under the derived id, so 'ddflow --agent sub-1 claim T1' from the parent's tree still adopts it (roborev probe on 61eb669: ADOPTED: True, branch parent-work). Needs a structured owner of a harness tree (e.g. recorded at first claim/adoption or session start from that tree) rather than inference from which id happened to write. Design choice: operator decision.

MCP refusals render an all-null result object: a refused ddflow_claim returns content[0] = {item: null, holder: null, worktree: null, ...} and isError false, with the reason only in a second text block and exit 3 only in _meta. A subagent reads the nulls as a broken success (home-simulator Bf05ce67c54's second ask). Probe on 5d02642: Server(called_from=tree); claim T1 (adopts); claim T2 -> {'item': null, ... } + 'this worktree is already bound to T1' and _meta.exit 3. Expected: a refusal's first block is the refusal (outcome refused, reason, exit 3), not the success schema filled with nulls.
